levels.title: Licensing wants albums and labels information
levels.task: The operations team just added a second table called album_info. Each row contains an album name and label. Join the top_songs table to album_info using the album_name column. Show all columns from both tables. Keep every song from top_songs, even if there is no matching album in album_info.
levels.solution: SELECT * FROM top_songs LEFT JOIN album_info ON top_songs.album_name = album_info.album_name;
levels.hintMessage: LEFT JOIN the top_songs and album_info tables on the album_name column.
levels.successMessage: Great job! You joined the two tables on the album_name column and selected all the columns from both tables.

levels.title: Only songs with label rows
levels.task: Someone on the festival marketing squad wants only the songs that have a matching album in album_info. Show all rows where top_songs has a matching album in album_info.
levels.solution: SELECT * FROM top_songs INNER JOIN album_info ON top_songs.album_name = album_info.album_name;
levels.hintMessage: INNER JOIN the top_songs and album_info tables on the album_name column.
levels.successMessage: Great job! You joined the two tables for albums that have a label.

levels.title: Top five: track and label
levels.task: Tour operations is printing wristbands for the first 5 songs in the table (id between 1 and 5). For each of those rows, show track_name and label. Keep tracks even when the directory has no row for that album.
levels.solution:
SELECT track_name, label AS label
FROM top_songs
LEFT JOIN album_info ON top_songs.album_name = album_info.album_name
WHERE id BETWEEN 1 AND 5;
levels.hintMessage: LEFT JOIN album_info on the album_name column. Check where the id is between 1 and 5.
levels.successMessage: Great job! You joined the two tables for the top 5 songs and selected the track_name and label columns.

levels.title: Top five with a label match
levels.task: Stellar Sound is preparing VIP wristbands for the highest-ranked songs on the chart, but they can only make wristbands for albums that already have label details on file. From the top_songs table, return every column for songs ranked 1 through 5 where the album also appears in the album_info table. Use the top_songs and album_info tables. HINT: There will only be 3 rows returned.
levels.solution:
SELECT *
FROM top_songs
INNER JOIN album_info ON top_songs.album_name = album_info.album_name
WHERE id BETWEEN 1 AND 5;
levels.hintMessage: INNER JOIN album_info on album_name. WHERE id BETWEEN 1 AND 5. There will only be 3 rows retured
levels.successMessage: We only have wristbands for the top five songs that have a matching album in album_info.

levels.title: Long chart run plus label
levels.task: Radio partnerships wants a full song row for every track that has been on the chart at least 25 weeks and has a matching album in the label directory.
levels.solution:
SELECT *
FROM top_songs
INNER JOIN album_info ON top_songs.album_name = album_info.album_name
WHERE weeks_on_chart >= 25;
levels.hintMessage: INNER JOIN album_info on album_name. WHERE weeks_on_chart >= 25.
levels.successMessage: Radio has full rows for every long chart run that already has label info—ready to pitch without chasing paperwork first.
